title: How to Create a Website From Scratch: 10 Steps for Beginners
summary: Your website is often the first impression, here’s how to build a website from the ground up.
body_markdown:
[Turn your ideas into a website](https://www.wix.com/website-builder)[→](https://www.wix.com/website-builder) **|**[Claim your domain →](https://www.wix.com/domains)


You can


[create a website](https://www.wix.com/website-builder) from scratch with or without coding skills. Start with a template, use AI to build a site for you, write the code yourself or combine a custom design with tools that handle things like content, payments and bookings.


The best approach depends on what you want to build, your experience and how much technical work you're comfortable taking on. This guide walks you through the main options and 10 steps to creating a website, from planning your site to publishing it and keeping it running.


**Turn your idea into a business-ready website.** Choose a template or start with AI, make the design your own and add the tools you need to sell products, accept bookings and reach customers, all with Wix.

##


TL;DR: how to make a website


Creating a website starts with a plan. You'll need to choose how to build it, organize your pages, set up a domain and hosting, prepare your content and test everything before launch. This guide takes you through each step, from getting started to publishing, promoting and maintaining your site.


**You'll learn:**


-


How website builders, AI tools and coding compare


-


How to plan your site, organize its pages and choose a domain and hosting


-


How to design your site, create content and make it accessible


-


How to test and launch your website, then maintain and promote it


-


What it costs to build a website


-


How to build with Wix, from templates and AI tools to headless setups


##


Ways to build a website in 2026


There are eight common ways to build a website today. They differ in how much you build yourself, the skills you need and who looks after hosting and security. For most beginners, a website builder or an AI website builder is the quickest way to start a website.


If you already know your method,


skip ahead to the 10 steps .

###


Website builder with templates


Some website builders combine designer-made templates, hosting and optional business tools like payments and bookings in one platform, with a custom domain usually available on paid plans.


A


[drag-and-drop website builder](https://www.wix.com/builder/drag-and-drop) lets you move text, images and buttons exactly where you want them. You pick a


[website template](https://www.wix.com/website/templates) , swap in your own text and images and publish.


This is still the lowest-risk starting point for most people. With a


[no-code website builder](https://www.wix.com/builder/no-code) , you never touch code, and the platform handles updates, security and speed.


[www.wix.com How Can I Use a Website Template to Make a Website Discover how to use a website template to make a website quickly and easily.](https://www.wix.com/blog/how-to-use-a-website-template-to-make-a-website)


###


AI website builder


An


[AI website builder](https://www.wix.com/ai-website-builder) creates the first version of your site from a short description. You answer a few questions or write a prompt, and the tool generates pages, layout, text and images that you then edit.


AI gets you to a solid draft quickly, but plan time to edit it so the copy, photos and offers reflect your business.


**Learn more:**


[How to create a website with AI](https://www.wix.com/blog/how-to-design-a-website-with-ai)


###


AI chat assistants like ChatGPT and Claude


You can create a website by describing what you want in a chat. When connected to a website platform, an AI assistant can create a site there or help manage its content and features. Without that connection, it may generate code that you need to publish separately.


With Wix, for example, you can type "@Wix" in ChatGPT to generate a website, or use the Wix connector in Claude to manage a site's store, bookings and content.


**Read more:**


[How to publish a website](https://www.wix.com/blog/how-to-publish-a-website)


[www.wix.com How to create a website with an LLM: A step-by-step guide Learn How to create a website with an LLM in minutes. Discover step-by-step guidance to efficiently create a website with an LLM using AI tools.](https://www.wix.com/blog/how-to-create-a-website-with-an-llm)


###


Vibe coding and AI coding tools


Vibe coding means describing what you want in plain language and letting an AI tool write the code. Tools like Claude Code, Cursor or vibe coding platforms produce a working project from prompts, and you keep refining it by chatting.


The output is a code project, so it may still need debugging, a production build and a place to host it before it's a live website.


For beginners, the harder part is everything after the code: putting it online, connecting a domain, setting up a secure connection and adding payments or bookings.


**Learn more:**


[How to vibe code a website](https://www.wix.com/blog/how-to-vibe-code-a-website)


[www.wix.com How to upload a website and make it live How to upload a website step by step, from your files to a live site with a custom domain.](https://www.wix.com/blog/how-to-upload-a-website)


###


Content management system (CMS)


A content management system (CMS) lets you create, edit and organize website content without building every page from scratch. Many CMS platforms offer templates and extensions to customize your site's design and features, making them useful for blogs and content-heavy websites.


Depending on the platform, you can host the CMS yourself or use a hosted service. Self-hosted setups require more responsibility for hosting, updates and maintenance, while hosted platforms handle more of the technical work for you.


**Learn more:**


[Website builder vs CMS](https://www.wix.com/blog/website-builder-vs-cms)


###


Hand-coding with HTML, CSS and JavaScript


Hand-coding a website gives you full control over design and functionality. HTML structures the page, CSS styles it and JavaScript makes it interactive.


The trade-off is time and responsibility. You own responsiveness, accessibility and performance, and how much hosting and security work you take on depends on the hosting or deployment service you choose.


It's a good path if you want to learn web development as a skill, but rarely the fastest way to launch one business site.


###


Headless website


A headless website keeps the part visitors see (the design) separate from the part that stores content and handles orders, bookings and payments. The name comes from removing the "head", meaning the built-in front end, from the system that runs the business side.


Headless describes how a site is built, not where it's hosted: the two parts can run with different providers or on one platform that manages both.


This suits developers, agencies and AI builders who want a fully custom design without building a backend from scratch. If you're exploring this setup, understanding


[what is a headless CMS](https://www.wix.com/headless/cms) can help you decide if it fits your project.


[www.wix.com How to make a Wix Headless website: a step-by-step guide Build a custom frontend with an AI assistant and let Wix run the payments, CMS and backend.](https://www.wix.com/blog/how-to-make-a-wix-headless-website)


###


Hiring a professional to build a website


If you'd rather spend your time on the business than the build, a designer, developer or agency can make the technical decisions for you. You trade budget for time, and you should still agree upfront on who will update the site after launch.

###


01. Define your website's purpose


Every great site starts with a clear


[website purpose](https://www.wix.com/blog/what-is-the-purpose-of-a-website) . Are you selling products, sharing your expertise, building a community or showing off your work? Your goal shapes every decision that follows, from the build method you choose to layout, content and navigation.


####


Define who your website is for


Understanding your audience is just as important. Think about who will visit your website and what they need from it. Consider their goals, questions and what would help them choose your business. Talk to existing customers, run surveys or interview potential visitors to understand their needs instead of making assumptions.


####


Research your competitors' websites


Check websites in your space and compare their navigation, pricing clarity, calls to action and how they work on a phone. Then decide what your site brings that theirs don't, whether it's a product, a service or a different approach.


####


Set measurable website goals


Decide which metrics matter most, such as traffic, sign-ups, bookings or sales. These goals guide your strategy and show you what's working after launch. Note your budget and the features you need at launch too, since both narrow down which build method fits.


####


Define your brand identity


Your brand is the personality, voice and visual style visitors associate with you. Write down 3 to 5 words that describe how the site should feel (for example trustworthy, playful, minimal or bold).


As a starting point, pick a primary color, one or two accent colors and a font pairing that reinforces those words. Use them consistently on every page so visitors get the same impression wherever they land.


####


Types of websites to consider


Depending on your goals, here are some types of websites you might want to create:


-


**Business and**[ecommerce websites](https://www.wix.com/ecommerce/website) : Sell products, book services or share your offerings with clear pricing, testimonials and contact options.


-


[Blog](https://www.wix.com/start/blog) : Share stories, expertise or insights, organized into categories, with an easy way to subscribe.


-


**Creative and**[portfolio websites](https://www.wix.com/portfolio-website) : Show your work with galleries and case studies. Perfect for photographers, designers, writers and artists.


-


**Content and media** : Share videos, podcasts or stories with clear navigation and search.


-


**Educational: Offer lessons** ,


[PDFs](https://www.wix.com/wixel/resources/pdf-files) , videos or certifications, with log-ins if learners need to track progress.


-


**Personal and lifestyle** : Share your stories, events or portfolio with galleries and social links.


-


[Non-profit websites](https://www.wix.com/blog/best-nonprofit-websites) : For schools, nonprofits and community organizations, with donations, volunteer sign-ups and event details.


Some websites juggle more than one purpose, but your main goal should always take the lead. Cleverchefs, a catering company, uses its site to tell its brand story and drive bookings at the same time.


Expert tip from Ian Lawson, Head of User Experience at Slickplan:


> "Before jumping into design, take time to understand who your audience is and how they look for information. The most successful websites are built around clear user goals. Letting that insight guide everything from site structure to navigation to content hierarchy ensures visitors find what they need in as few clicks as possible."


###


02. Choose your website builder or build method


Now that you know the main ways to create a website, choose the approach that fits your goals, skills and budget. Website builders and AI website builders are often the easiest starting points for beginners, while coding, CMS platforms and headless setups offer other levels of control and flexibility.


If you choose a website builder, check what's included. Hosting is usually built in, while a custom domain may cost extra or be included with an eligible plan. Templates and design tools help you customize the look of your site, and built-in features can support online stores, bookings, memberships and email marketing.


AI tools can speed up the process by generating layouts, pages, content or code. What you get depends on the tool: it might be a website you can publish directly, a draft to customize or code that needs hosting and additional setup.


Before committing, check the platform's features, costs and maintenance requirements to make sure they fit the website you want to create.


**Worth knowing:** an AI-generated site is a starting point, not the finished product. Plan time to edit the generated copy, swap in your own photos and adjust layouts so the site sounds and looks like your brand.


**Key factors to compare before you commit:**


**Factor**


**What to look for**


**Customizability**


Flexible layouts, templates, AI-assisted site creation


**Technical control**


Access to code, data and hosting settings, if you need them (visual editors can be highly customizable without exposing code)


**Business tools**


Ecommerce, scheduling, inventory, CRM, automation


**AI capabilities**


What the AI produces (a draft, code or a live site) and how you edit it afterward


**Third-party integrations**


Apps, sales channels, marketing tools


**Security**


What's included on your plan: a secure connection (SSL), backups, monitoring, account protection


**Performance**


Fast loading worldwide, optimized code


**Support**


24/7 help, tutorials, guides


On Wix, for example, the


[Wix App Market](https://www.wix.com/app-market) adds third-party apps and sales channels, and


[Wix Headless](https://www.wix.com/headless) connects Wix business tools to a site you built elsewhere.


Expert tip from Rebecca Tomasis, Head of Organic Growth Marketing at Wix:


> "A website builder should remove operational friction, not add to it. The easier it is to update, expand and optimize your site from one platform, the faster your business can respond to new opportunities."


###


03. Pick and register a domain name


Your domain is your web address, the


[URL](https://www.wix.com/blog/what-is-a-url) visitors type to find your site. Behind the scenes, the


[Domain Name System](https://www.wix.com/blog/what-is-the-domain-name-system-dns) (DNS) uses records to point that name to your site's


[IP address](https://www.wix.com/blog/what-is-an-ip-internet-protocol-address) , so your website loads for anyone who visits. DNS also holds other records, such as the ones that route your email.


A strong domain name is unique, memorable and easy to spell. Avoid long or complicated names, numbers or special characters. A


[domain name generator](https://www.wix.com/domains/domain-name-generator) can give you creative ideas and check availability quickly.


Think about the right


[domain extension](https://www.wix.com/domains/tld-list) for your website, such as .com, .co, .store, .info or .digital. Choose one that fits your brand and audience, since a matching custom domain helps your site look established.


####


Claim your domain


Next, claim your domain through a registrar. Domains are registered for a set period (commonly a year, though options vary by extension), and


[domain pricing](https://www.wix.com/domains/domain-pricing) covers


[domain registration](https://www.wix.com/domains) and DNS services behind it. Many website builders, including Wix, offer a


[free domain](https://www.wix.com/domains/free-domain) for the first year with eligible paid plans.


Before you buy, check the renewal price after the first year, since it's often different from the opening price, and turn on auto-renewal so you don't lose the domain.


To register a domain:


-


Brainstorm 5 to 10 short, memorable names that are easy to spell


-


Check availability with a


[domain name search](https://www.wix.com/domains/domain-name-search)


-


Choose an extension that fits your brand, like


[.com, .net or .org](https://www.wix.com/blog/org-vs-com-vs-net-domain-extensions)


-


Register your domain (most extensions start at one year), or claim a free domain with a plan that includes one


-


Use accurate contact details and turn on two-step verification for your account


-


Connect the domain to your website and update its DNS settings


Registering, connecting and transferring are separate actions. Registering buys the name, connecting points it to your site and transferring moves it to a different registrar, even when one platform handles all three.


**Learn more:**


[What is a custom domain?](https://www.wix.com/blog/what-are-custom-domains)


###


04. Choose a web hosting plan


[Web hosting](https://www.wix.com/free/web-hosting) stores your site's files, images and content on a server so visitors can reach your site online. Every time someone enters your URL, the server delivers your pages.


It helps to keep three things apart: the domain is the address, hosting is what makes your files available online and the website is the pages, content and features visitors use. Registering a domain doesn't publish anything by itself; it has to be connected to a hosted site.


If you use a website builder, hosting is usually bundled, so this step may already be done. For a site built in code, choose hosting once you know what the site needs to run.


When you evaluate hosting, consider uptime, security, speed and support. The hosting type alone doesn't decide performance: configuration, caching, a content delivery network (servers around the world that keep copies of your pages) and your site's own code matter too.


####


Hosting a website you built with code or AI


If you've already built a site with code or an AI tool, you may be able to upload the finished files directly.


With Wix Headless, for example, you can


[drag and drop your HTML, CSS and JavaScript files](https://www.wix.com/headless/drop) (up to 20MB in total) to get managed hosting, a secure connection and fast loading worldwide. Projects that need a build step or server-side code need a compatible deployment setup instead.


**Hosting type**


**Best for**


**What you get**


**Shared hosting**


Beginners, small websites


Low cost and easy setup; performance depends on the provider and your neighbors on the server


**VPS hosting**


Growing businesses


A reserved share of server resources and more configuration control


**Cloud hosting**


Sites with changing traffic


Resources that can scale with demand, depending on how it's set up


**Managed hosting (often bundled with builders)**


Owners who don't want to run servers


The provider runs the hosting infrastructure and agreed maintenance; who updates your site's apps or plugins varies


**Dedicated hosting**


Large enterprises


A whole physical server and full control, with full responsibility for configuring it


These labels overlap: shared, VPS, cloud and dedicated describe how server resources are arranged, while managed describes who operates them.


###


05. Design your site: pick a template or start with AI


Before you start building, think about how you want your website to look and feel. You can start with a template, let AI create a first version or design it yourself from scratch.


####


How to design a website with a template


Start by browsing professional


website templates


, and choose one for its structure and features as well as its looks. Templates give you a design foundation, but you can make every part your own: layouts, section order, spacing, fonts, colors, buttons, images, headers, footers, menus, backgrounds and animations.


Preview the template on mobile before you commit, since layouts can shift on small screens. You can discover more in this piece:


[Should I use a template to make a website](https://www.wix.com/blog/should-i-use-a-template-to-build-a-website) ?


**Check out these templates to get building:**


-


[Website templates for designers](https://www.wix.com/website/templates/html/design)


-


[Portfolio templates](https://www.wix.com/website/templates/html/portfolio-cv/portfolios)


-


[Landing page templates](https://www.wix.com/website/templates/html/one-page/landing-pages)


-


[Blog templates](https://www.wix.com/website/templates/html/blog)


-


[Simple website templates](https://www.wix.com/blog/simple-website-templates)


Expert tip from Hani Safe, product lead (Showcase) at Wix:


> "Beautiful templates let creators bring their stories to life, ensuring that every website not only stands out for its aesthetic appeal but also tells a compelling story about the creator behind it."


####


How to design a website with AI


An AI website builder can generate an initial design from a written prompt. Describe your business, target audience and the site's main goal, then specify the visual style you want, such as minimalist, bold or editorial. List the pages you need, like Home, Services, About and Contact, and include any key features, such as a booking form or product gallery. You can also share reference websites to help guide the design.


Once the AI generates your site, review the layout, navigation and content rather than accepting the first version. Replace placeholder images with your own visuals, rewrite generic copy to reflect your brand and adjust colors, fonts and spacing. If something feels off, give the AI specific feedback about what to change instead of starting over with a new prompt.


Finally, check how the design works on mobile and desktop. Make sure text is readable, buttons are easy to tap and menus and forms work as expected. AI can speed up the initial design, but you'll still need to review and refine the result before publishing.


[www.wix.com How to make a quick website easily (with and without AI) Everything you need to understand how to create a website fast, with and without AI.](https://www.wix.com/blog/how-to-make-a-website-fast)


####


Designing a site built in code


If you're building with an AI coding tool, describe the look and feel you want, including your brand colors, fonts, layout and reference sites. You can also create a mockup in a visual design tool first, then use it to guide the AI as it generates your pages.


Review the result and refine it until the design feels consistent across your site. Check every page on desktop and mobile, paying attention to navigation, spacing, text readability and elements that overlap or break on smaller screens.


If you're writing the code yourself, use HTML to structure the content, CSS to control the design and JavaScript to add interactive features.


Whichever path you choose, treat the first version as a draft and keep refining it until it looks and sounds like your brand.


####


Gather inspiration for any approach


Check competitor websites and visual platforms like Pinterest and Instagram for fonts, colors and design styles. Learn from the patterns, but don't copy another site's photos, logos, text or distinctive design.


**Explore real websites made with Wix:**


-


[Website ideas](https://www.wix.com/explore/websites)


-


[Portfolio website ideas](https://www.wix.com/explore/websites/categories/portfolio)


-


[Ecommerce website design inspiration](https://www.wix.com/explore/websites/categories/ecommerce)


###


06. Build your site structure


A beautiful website won't succeed if visitors can't navigate it easily. Start with a clear site structure by creating a sitemap, the blueprint for your pages, and organize content into logical sections that match your goals and audience. Some website builders update the sitemap automatically as you add pages, so check how yours handles it.


Before you build, sketch each key page roughly: where the headline sits, what a visitor sees first and where the main button goes. A pen-and-paper wireframe is enough, and it matters most when you build with someone else, because it surfaces layout disagreements early.


Next, optimize your navigation menu. Make important pages easy to reach without unnecessary steps; a common rule of thumb is to keep key pages within about three clicks of the homepage. Prioritize your homepage, services, products and contact details, and add a clickable logo that returns visitors to the homepage.


Large sites can use well-organized mega menus, while smaller ones often work best with an anchor menu that scrolls to sections on one page.


Expert tip from Adi Huri, Head of Product and Creative Director for WOW, Wix's Visual Innovation Team:


> "Think of the menu as the map of your website. Adding the right pages in the right order can make it the heart of your site's success."


Highlight your most important content, including services, pricing and contact details, and use clear calls to action to guide visitors toward sign-ups, bookings or purchases. Use the footer for extra links, social profiles and legal pages.


Plan for growth with flexible layouts that make adding pages or features easy, and review your structure regularly as the site grows.


**Site structure checklist**


**Step**


**Action**


**Tip**


**Sitemap**


Map all your pages into logical sections


Check whether your platform updates the sitemap automatically


**Navigation menu**


Link main pages, use clear categories


Keep key pages easy to reach from the main menu


**Key content**


Highlight services, pricing, contact info, use CTAs


Combine analytics with usability tests and visitor feedback


**Footer**


Add extra links, contact info, social profiles


Keep legal and policy pages here


**Scalability**


Use flexible layouts, plan for growth


Review site structure as you add pages; layout and structure can evolve together


###


07. Add useful pages


Once you've mapped out your pages, it's time to create them. Most sites use some combination of these


[web pages](https://www.wix.com/blog/what-is-a-webpage-vs-a-website) , depending on their purpose:


-


**An inviting**[homepage](https://www.wix.com/blog/what-is-a-homepage) **:** the face of your website. Present the crucial elements right away so visitors instantly understand who you are and what you do.


-


**A shop or gallery:** where visitors browse your products or services. Write product descriptions that grab attention and use photography that shows your items in their best light.


-


**A personable About page:** your


[online business card](https://www.wix.com/tools/business-card-maker) . Share who you are, what you stand for and what makes your team or business different.


-


**An easy-to-find contact section:** list phone numbers, email, social links and any other way to reach you, and repeat the essentials in your footer.


-


**An engaging blog:** by


[starting a blog](https://www.wix.com/blog/how-to-start-a-blog) , you add fresh content regularly, show your expertise and support your SEO.


You can also consider adding these pages:


-


Membership area


-


Online courses


-


FAQ page


-


Online booking system


-


Testimonials page


-


Custom 404 page


####


Legal and policy pages


If your site collects personal information, uses cookies, takes payments or sells products, you'll likely need pages like a privacy policy, a cookie notice, terms of service and shipping, returns and refund policies.


What's required depends on where your business and visitors are, so check the rules that apply to you (this isn't legal advice).


###


08. Create engaging website content


Your website content should grab attention and keep visitors interested, so focus on variety, clarity and structure. Mix text, photos, videos and animations, and place your most important content above the fold (the part visible without scrolling) so visitors see your value immediately.


Structure matters. Use clear headers, concise text and visuals like images or infographics to make content easy to scan, and avoid long blocks of text or too many effects.


Use images you have the rights to: your own photos, licensed stock or AI-generated images whose terms allow commercial use.


Expert tip from Amanda Weiner, GEO/AEO Team Lead at Wix:


> "Site hierarchy and the information you provide your visitors with is more than just how your site looks. It directly impacts how many visitors ultimately buy your products. Be clear about your offerings through your content, visuals and buttons right from the get go."


Once your content is ready, optimize it for search engines with titles, descriptions and clear headings. Built-in tools like


[Wix SEO](https://www.wix.com/seo) guide you through this page by page.


Your content also needs to work on phones. According to


[StatCounter GlobalStats](https://www.statista.com/statistics/277125/share-of-website-traffic-coming-from-mobile-devices/) , mobile devices account for the majority of global web traffic. Choose mobile-friendly templates and check every page on a phone before you publish.


####


Make your site accessible


An accessible site is one that everyone can use, including visitors with low vision, mobility limitations or screen readers.


Add descriptive alt text to meaningful images (purely decorative images can have empty alt text), use color contrast that meets accessibility guidelines, keep body text comfortably large (many designers use 16 pixels or more) and make sure every interactive element works with a keyboard.


Accessibility tools can scan your site for common issues; Wix, for example, includes an


[Accessibility Wizard](https://www.wix.com/accessibility) . An automated scan can't confirm full accessibility or compliance with your region's laws on its own, so for regulated or high-risk sites, have an accessibility expert review the result.


The stakes are rising in Europe. The European Accessibility Act has applied since June 2025 to specific products and services, including many ecommerce services. It doesn't cover every website the same way, and microenterprises that provide services are exempt, so check which rules apply to your business.


In a


[Level Access](https://levelaccess.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/The-State-of-Digital-Accessibility-in-Europe.pdf) survey of more than 500 enterprise leaders in Germany, France, Italy and the U.K., 87% said the EAA applies to their organization, but only 66% had begun taking action to comply.


####


What makes a great website


**What it includes**


**Why it matters**


**Clear purpose**


Helps visitors quickly understand what your site offers


**Easy navigation**


Makes it easy for people to find what they need


**Fast load time**


Keeps visitors engaged


**Consistent branding**


Builds trust and makes your site look professional


**High-quality content**


Provides value and encourages action


**Strong visual website design**


Captures attention and reflects your unique brand


**SEO optimization**


Helps your site show up when people search

09. Test and launch your website


Before publishing, make sure your site is ready with a few key checks.


####


Preview your site


Use your builder's preview mode to experience the site as a visitor would, checking navigation, layout and design. Check it on smartphones and tablets, and proofread all text for spelling, grammar and clarity.


####


Test functionality


Test every page, link, button and embedded video on both desktop and mobile. Submit each form to confirm the messages actually arrive, check that your domain connects with a secure connection (https) and make sure your analytics records visits.


####


Test payments and bookings


If your site sells or takes bookings, run the real customer flow before launch:


-


Complete a test purchase or booking from start to finish


-


Check that confirmation emails and notifications arrive


-


Confirm prices, taxes, shipping and availability display correctly


-


Make cancellation, refund and contact details easy to find


-


See what happens when a payment fails or a required field is empty


####


Cross-browser check


Check your site on popular browsers like Chrome, Firefox and Safari to make sure it displays correctly for everyone.


####


Check your load speed


There's no single pass or fail load time, but Google's Core Web Vitals give useful benchmarks. Largest Contentful Paint, the moment the main content appears, should be


[2.5 seconds or less](https://web.dev/articles/lcp) for most visits.


The other two Core Web Vitals measure how quickly the page responds to taps and clicks and how stable the layout stays while it loads. Test on a mobile connection rather than office Wi-Fi, using a free tool like PageSpeed Insights.


The usual causes of slow pages are oversized images and heavy video. Upload images at the size they're displayed, use modern formats, let images lower on the page load as visitors scroll (lazy loading) and keep autoplaying video off the homepage.


Platforms that serve your site from servers around the world and optimize images automatically cover much of this, but run a real test before you publish.


####


Get feedback


Ask a friend, colleague or team member to navigate the site and give feedback on usability, clarity and design, then make final tweaks.


When your site is ready, hit Publish and check that search engines can index it: confirm your settings allow indexing, verify the site in Google Search Console, submit a sitemap and watch the Page Indexing report.


Google can also find sites on its own, and none of these steps guarantees indexing or rankings, which can take time.


In your Wix


SEO


Settings, for example, this is the "Let search engines index your site" toggle, and the Wix SEO Setup Checklist walks you through the rest. You'll also get a complete


[website launch checklist](https://www.wix.com/blog/website-launch-checklist) to make sure every detail is ready before you hit publish.


Expert tip from Dafna Rabin, Wix Templates Design Team Lead:


> "It's a simple test: publish your website, scroll through it and ensure everything is visible and nothing is missing or out of place. Don't forget to check the mobile version as well, which is often overlooked. This applies to every website, not just business websites."

10. Maintain and promote your website


[Update your website](https://www.wix.com/blog/how-to-update-a-website) regularly by adding new content and keeping existing pages current to improve navigation, SEO and overall performance.

Track performance

####


Listen to your audience


Collect feedback through surveys, forms or conversations, and combine it with your analytics to refine navigation, content and features.


####


Protect your site


A secure connection (SSL) encrypts data between your site and visitors, but it doesn't protect against everything. Use strong passwords, two-step verification and user roles that control who can edit what, keep any apps or plugins updated and only collect the personal data you need.


Check what your backups cover (pages, store data, media) and how far back you can restore, so you can roll back after a failed update or an accidental deletion.


On managed platforms, the provider handles much of the infrastructure. Wix, for example, monitors sites for threats, encrypts data with SSL/TLS and saves previous versions of your site that you can restore.


You're still responsible for your content, account access and any privacy obligations that apply to your business.

A simple schedule keeps small problems from piling up. Adjust the timing to how busy your site is:

**Weekly:** check that forms, orders and bookings are coming through


-


**Monthly:** review analytics, fix broken links and update outdated content


-


**Every few months:** review who has access, test restoring a backup and update apps and integrations

Marketing often adds more than the website itself, so plan for ongoing promotion. Start small, scale later and keep content and design updated.

##


How to create a website from scratch FAQ


###


Can anyone create a website from scratch?


Yes. "From scratch" can mean starting from a template, generating a site with AI or writing the code yourself, and the first two need no coding. Managed platforms like Wix handle hosting, a secure connection (HTTPS) and most technical maintenance, while you stay responsible for your content, account security and any legal requirements that apply to your site.


###


Can a beginner build a website?


Definitely. Today's website builders are designed for beginners with no coding experience. With drag-and-drop editors, pre-designed templates and step-by-step guidance, anyone can create a professional-looking website. The most important part is having a clear vision for your brand and what you want your site to achieve.


###


Can I create my own website for free?


Yes. Platforms like Wix let you build and publish a site without any upfront cost. A free plan usually uses a platform subdomain, shows platform branding and has feature limits, so you can upgrade to a paid plan for a custom domain and advanced features as your needs grow.


###


Do I need to buy a domain before building a website?


No. Most website builders let you build, and even publish, on a free platform subdomain first, then connect a custom domain when you're ready. If you already have a name in mind, register it early so no one else takes it.


###


What is the easiest way to build a website?


For most beginners, the easiest way is a website builder that includes hosting, a domain and templates, or an AI website builder that creates a first draft from a short description. Both let you publish without code and edit everything afterward.


###


How do I create a website for my business?


Start with what the site needs to do for customers, such as showing your services, taking bookings or selling products. Then choose a platform with the business features you need built in, register a domain that matches your business name and add the essentials: a clear homepage, services or products, an About page, contact details and any required policy pages. Test everything on mobile before you launch.


###


Can AI build a website for me?


Yes, though the result depends on the tool. AI website builders and assistants connected to a website platform can generate an editable, publishable site, while AI coding tools produce a code project you still need to test and host. Either way, review the content, add your own photos and adjust details so the site reflects your brand.


###


Do websites make money?


They can, and many do. A website can generate income by selling products or services, offering paid memberships, running ads or through affiliate marketing. Whether it pays off depends on demand for your offer, steady traffic, a monetization model that fits your audience and keeping costs below what the site earns.


###


What are common challenges faced during a website launch?


Common challenges include unclear goals, missing content, broken links, slow loading times, domain connection issues, search engine indexing turned off and missing privacy or policy pages. Many first-time creators also skip testing on different devices before publishing. A short pre-launch checklist and built-in analytics help you catch these early.
